classification.difficultyReason: Requires an angle-sum equation, algebraic solution and substitution to prove that two angles are equal.

content.prompt: Show that this triangle is isosceles.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 14 triangle beneath the prompt on the left.
spec.description: Unshaded triangle with a horizontal base, upper apex and three interior-angle arcs. No printed vertex names or equal-side marks.
spec.mathematics: Apex angle (4a+16)°, bottom-left angle (3a+29)°, bottom-right angle (4a−8)°. Drawing proportions do not supply side equality.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no solved values or proof annotations appear.

answer.short: $a=13$. The angles $3a+29$ and $4a+16$ are both $68^\circ$, so the triangle is isosceles.
answer.worked:
Angles in a triangle sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}(3a+29)+(4a+16)+(4a-8)&=180\\11a+37&=180\\11a&=143\\a&=13\end{align*}$$
Substituting $a=13$:
$$\begin{align*}3a+29&=3(13)+29\\&=68\\4a+16&=4(13)+16\\&=68\end{align*}$$
Two angles are equal to $68^\circ$, so their opposite sides are equal. Therefore the triangle is isosceles.
